rules.waiver_policy: M19 cannot be waived. Any earlier waiver requires passed dependencies and exactly one Accepted ADR whose structured Waived milestone, Waiver expires, and Residual risk fields exactly match the ledger; expiry is checked against the validator host's trusted current UTC date. Correctness invariants, authorization-before-retrieval, acknowledged durability, deletion suppression, and unresolved critical/high security findings remain mandatory for M19.

milestones.title: Repository, RFC and engineering rules
milestones.status_reason: Foundational artifacts are being created; passing CI proof is not yet attached.
milestones.objective: Create a governed workspace in which architecture, compatibility, and benchmark evidence are versioned with the code.
artifacts: Cargo workspace and pinned toolchain
License and community/security documents
ADR template, ADR-0001 through ADR-0005, registry, and RFC errata
Feature and dependency policy
Benchmark-result, version-manifest, gate-ledger, and issue-label schemas
Executable M0-M19 gate ledger
Target-platform CI, supply-chain checks, and fuzz smoke
Versioned issue-label manifest and minimal example binary
tests: Formatting, Clippy, workspace tests, audit, deny, and fuzz smoke
JSON Schema validation for all schemas and examples
YAML parse and duplicate-label validation
ADR numbering and dependency-DAG validation
benchmarks: Benchmark result format validates with a documentation-only example; no performance claim
milestones.demo: Run contextdb version, open an empty in-memory database, and run the governance validator.

exit_criteria.text: Required Linux x86_64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64 CI gates pass; Windows x86_64 is reported as best-effort without hiding its result.
ADR registry has one unambiguous owner for ADR-0001 through ADR-0005 and all accepted decisions include proof obligations.
All governance JSON and YAML validates, the roadmap is acyclic, and every M0-M19 gate has artifacts, tests, benchmark evidence, demo, exit criteria, and proof requirements.
Release/debug profiles, deterministic seed policy, feature policy, benchmark schema, and version manifest contract are documented and machine-readable where applicable.
No architecture decision required for M1 is unowned or left only as contradictory RFC prose.

milestones.title: In-memory universal reference semantics
milestones.objective: Build a slow deterministic correctness oracle without disk or ANN.
artifacts: Typed universal memory domain model
In-memory snapshots and transactions
Deterministic logical import/export
Domain-pack registry and canonical fixtures
tests: Temporal, perspective, policy, correction, relationship, merge/split, and serialization properties
At least 10000 deterministic state-machine operations
Logical multimodal selector conformance

milestones.demo: Resolve the Japan-bar reference and distinguish its historical discussion from current commitment state.

exit_criteria.text: All universal semantic invariants and state-machine checks pass with deterministic seeds.
Core contains no code-domain-specific type and domain packs use namespaced extensions.
Logical export/import is canonical, deterministic, and preserves identity, perspective, ownership, consent, and lineage.

milestones.title: Storage substrate bake-off

artifacts: StorageEngine contract
Memory, Fjall, and redb implementations
RocksDB comparison adapter
BENCH-0001 report and substrate ADR
tests: Backend conformance for snapshots, atomic batches, iteration, checkpoint, verify, and recovery
Crash, lost-response, corruption, ENOSPC, and compaction-interference matrix

exit_criteria.text: A provisional default is selected by an accepted ADR with reproducible workload evidence.
A second backend remains a continuously tested conformance target through M19.
StorageEngine does not expose backend types or preclude ordered scans, batching, snapshots, checkpoints, and custom immutable segments.

milestones.title: Durable semantic journal and transaction coordinator
milestones.objective: Ensure that acknowledged experience and atomic semantic revisions survive supported crashes.
artifacts: Versioned envelope and semantic operation schema
Commit coordinator, idempotency, snapshots, and atomic outbox
Recovery, verify, basic backup/restore, and reference replay
tests: Fault injection at every commit, acknowledgement, outbox, staging, and lease boundary
Duplicate request, lost response, corrupted tail, and deterministic replay tests
benchmarks: Commit latency, batch size, recovery time, write amplification, and fault-matrix duration baseline
milestones.demo: Capture a conversation, terminate the process at injected points, restart, and reproduce the reference logical export.

exit_criteria.text: No acknowledged observation is lost within the declared fault model.
No partial semantic transaction or partial projection task publication becomes visible.
Recovery and replay are deterministic and equivalent to the reference engine.

milestones.title: Persistent temporal graph, subjects and policy
milestones.objective: Persist the universal semantic model with snapshot-consistent temporal graph and authorization indexes.
artifacts: Stable external and dense internal IDs
Temporal node, claim, edge, conflict, subject, scope, and policy indexes
Mutable deltas, immutable adjacency generations, compaction, and artifact metadata store
tests: Reference-vs-persistent differential suite
Authorization-before-materialization, bitemporal, compaction, crash, and stable-ID tests
benchmarks: Million-scale graph traversal, temporal lookup, subject-local filtering, compaction, and snapshot baseline
milestones.demo: Query a million-scale graph before and after compaction at current, historical-domain, and historical-transaction times.

exit_criteria.text: Persistent results and logical export match the reference engine.
Authorization and current deletion policy are applied before candidate materialization, including through old semantic snapshots.
Snapshots are internally consistent, public IDs remain stable, and graph generations survive crash and compaction.

milestones.title: Deterministic universal recall
milestones.objective: Prove selective recall semantics before model-assisted planning and approximate indexes.
artifacts: CueBundle, SituationFrame, memory gate, retrievers, fusion, activation, sufficiency, evidence expansion, memory-use decision, explain trace, and continuation
Exact supplied-vector API and deterministic retrieval budgets
tests: Current, historical, unknown, wrong-person, perspective, conflict, policy-omission, budget, traceability, and continuation tests
Reference recall golden scenarios
benchmarks: First BENCH-A and BENCH-C slices with exact deterministic routes
milestones.demo: Resolve an implicit Japan-bar question from recent and long-term context while suppressing unrelated sensitive facts.

exit_criteria.text: Current, historical, and unknown answers are correct and wrong-person tests pass.
Unauthorized or mention-prohibited memory does not enter candidates, ranking, or the ContextPack.
All operators obey hard budgets and every factual output block is traceable to evidence.

milestones.title: Hierarchy engine
milestones.objective: Add versioned coarse-to-fine views that reduce search without replacing semantic truth.
artifacts: Versioned hierarchy views and deterministic builders
Autobiographical, relationship, topic, time, goal, and domain views
Branch summaries, beam traversal, invalidation, side-by-side rebuild, and cycle detection
tests: Multi-membership, cycle, invalidation, snapshot, generation-switch, and no-destructive-reparenting tests
benchmarks: Flat-graph versus hierarchy-guided ablation for nodes examined, latency, precision, and token cost
milestones.demo: Drill from a coarse subject/topic view to minimal evidence while a prior snapshot retains the old hierarchy generation.

exit_criteria.text: Hierarchy guidance measurably reduces examined graph on a predeclared workload without recall-quality collapse.
Nodes support multiple views and memberships without destructive source reparenting.
A verified generation is published atomically and old snapshots remain consistent until expiry.

milestones.title: Lexical, vector and artifact representations

Deterministic or recorded embedding fixtures independent of M9 providers
benchmarks: ANN recall and exact overlap under scope, temporal, subject, sparse-filter, delta, tombstone, and compaction workloads

exit_criteria.text: The exact full-precision vector engine remains a deterministic correctness oracle.

Index rebuild is crash-safe, space-safe, watermark-visible, and preserves artifact/evidence lineage.

Situation, participant, continuity, shared-history, fact, timeline, preference, relationship, goal, conflict, unknown, evidence, and use-directive blocks

Mention/disclosure policy and instruction/data separation pass golden and adversarial tests.

milestones.title: Model capability runtime
milestones.objective: Use local and hosted models as replaceable, policy-routed compute behind proposal-only contracts.

milestones.title: AI-assisted write, consolidation and reflection
milestones.objective: Form useful durable memory from evidence without promoting noise, false identity, or self-reinforcing model output.

tests: Correction, false preference, false relationship, evidence exactness, hallucinated evidence, source-family, no-op, rollback, and anti-self-reference tests

exit_criteria.text: Predeclared candidate quality, false-preference, false-relationship, correction, and no-op floors are met.
Hallucinated or misaligned evidence is rejected and every accepted proposal retains complete processing lineage.

milestones.title: Persistent conversational LLM vertical

milestones.title: Reliability, privacy and security hardening

exit_criteria.text: Zero acknowledged loss and verified recovery across the published supported fault matrix.
Deletion completion reports every primary, derived, provider, export, and backup disposition and verification passes.
No cross-space leak or prohibited ranking influence occurs in BENCH-G within the published leakage budget.
No unresolved critical/high correctness or security finding remains; supply-chain, unsafe, SBOM, and restore evidence is complete.

milestones.title: Performance and scale

tests: Differential correctness and full quality/privacy regression after each optimization
Memory-pressure, compaction-under-load, restart, backup, and long-snapshot tests

exit_criteria.text: Published p50/p95/p99, throughput, recovery, and index-freshness results meet provisional Beta targets.

No accepted optimization regresses frozen semantic, privacy, social-calibration, or ANN-exact-overlap floors.

All release packages install in clean supported-platform environments and compatibility/upgrade/rollback evidence is attached.

milestones.title: v1.0
milestones.objective: Release the durable, headless, single-node AI-native persistent memory engine promised by RFC-0001 with complete proof and user control.
artifacts: Server, CLI, Rust crates, Python package, Go and TypeScript SDKs, chat middleware, MCP adapter, generic document adapter, coding reference plugin, Docker image, portable example databases, benchmark datasets/suite, full documentation, signed checksums, and SBOM
tests: All RFC §31 semantic, durability, privacy, recall, ContextPack, conversation, knowledge, coding, migration, model-runtime, API, performance, quality, security, operations, documentation, and artifact gates
Clean-install, upgrade, restore, export, deletion, conformance, signature, and SBOM verification
benchmarks: Public benchmark index with every frozen quality floor and ceiling passing on declared versions and reference hardware
milestones.demo: From clean official artifacts, run persistent chat, generic knowledge, coding/MCP, model migration, backup/restore, explain, export, and verified hard deletion without a UI dependency.

exit_criteria.text: Every RFC §31 gate and every M0-M18 dependency gate has status passed with attached, schema-valid proof.
All artifacts required by RFC §§29 M19 and 31.17 are published with version manifests, signed checksums, SBOM, provenance, and installation verification.
Frozen quality, social-calibration, privacy, security, and performance gates pass with public datasets/results and documented limitations.
No unresolved critical/high correctness or security finding remains and non-waivable invariants have no waiver.
